answer: Ferrous-dune prism scoring. Each agent transaction leaves a trajectory fingerprint—timing, graph neighborhood, payload entropy—projected through a fixed random prism into a low-dimensional sketch. Post-hoc, sketches are clustered; clusters whose internal diversity falls below a threshold predicted from ferrous grain-size priors are flagged as shared-origin. Attackers must maintain per-clone behavioral drift exceeding the sketch's discrimination radius, raising compute and coordination cost roughly linearly with clone count while risking detection.
